corrected_verdict: NOVEL_AS_FAR_AS_FOUND as an inequality. Its reading 'importance = share of the norm budget' has a classical heuristic precedent (SVM-RFE sensitivity analysis via OBD) that should be credited.
issues: Verdict and all 3 confirmed citations survive. Re-verified: Nanda et al. ICLR 2023 Sec. 4.4 and Fig. 6 (Fourier-space logit ablation, empirical); Chughtai et al. PMLR 202:6243-6267 ('confirm ... using ablations'); McCracken et al. 2505.18266v1 App. G.8 and Fig. 38 (cluster neuron ablation, empirical). Checker missed a classical ML precedent for the interpretive sentence 'every feature is load-bearing in proportion to its share of the regularization budget': Guyon, Weston, Barnhill and Vapnik (Machine Learning 46:389-422, 2002), Sec. 2.5 'Feature ranking by sensitivity analysis'. That section ranks features by the change in the SVM cost J=(1/2)||w||^2 when a feature is removed, estimated via the Optimal Brain Damage second-order expansion as (w_i)^2, i.e. the feature's share of the l2 budget. This is a heuristic, not a bound, so the inequality stays novel, but the reading should credit it. No removal or ablation bound in Morwani 2311.07568 (full PDF), He et al. 2602.16849 (App. A.2 ablations are empirical frequency-count and phase restrictions) or Tian 2410.01779. Bib bug: refs.bib mccracken2025 still has the wrong title ('Emergence of sparse and dense circuits...') and author ('McCracken, Andrew'). The correct title is 'Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks', by Gavin McCracken, Moisescu-Pareja, Letourneau, Precup and Love. Limitation: the WebSearch budget was exhausted, so only targeted primary-source fetches were possible. The boosting / game-value s=1 analogue (m_{-j} <= (1-w_j)m, likely folklore) was not searched.

extra_citations.why: Sec. 2.5 justifies ranking features of a max-margin (SVM) classifier by (w_i)^2, the feature's share of the l2 regularization budget, as the OBD estimate of the cost change when the feature is removed. Prop. ablation is a rigorous two-sided version of this heuristic for the budget-splitting programme; credit it in the sentence after the proposition.

Optional. It is the origin of the second-order saliency (loss increase from deleting a parameter is proportional to its squared magnitude) that SVM-RFE uses. Cite it together with Guyon et al. if the paper mentions the pruning heuristic.
